text: In Parfit's fission case, your two brain hemispheres are transplanted into two different bodies, each waking with your psychology. Parfit's own conclusion is that:
choices: you survive as exactly one of the two people, though we cannot know which
you die, because neither successor has any of what matters in survival
the case shows that bodily, not psychological, continuity constitutes identity
since you cannot be identical to two distinct people yet both have what matters, identity is not what matters -- psychological continuity (Relation R) is
explanation: Fission gives you everything that matters (full psychological continuity) twice over, yet strict identity fails because identity is one-one. Parfit concludes we should stop caring about identity as such and care about Relation R. Options 0 and 1 are resolutions Parfit rejects; option 2 is the animalist response, not Parfit's.
